text:
lina: FYI — StormWave came back with numbers for Dedicated. They want a contracted pool for eu-west with predictable latency and a ~monthly commit. They attached a spreadsheet, but main ask is 45k GPU hours/month plus a 25% headroom.

mike: Good catch. Are they asking for a hard buffer (i.e., reserved buffer that counts against our capacity) or flexible burst credits?

tom-stormwave: mike hi — we need the headroom to avoid throttling during marketing pushes. We can accept burst that has a short warmup but want firm p95 latency targets. Prefer a single EU region.

sarah: quick note — eu-west currently has two constrained racks for A100s next quarter. We can guarantee base commit but sustained 25% hard buffer is tough without cannibalizing other Dedicated pools.

lina: what's the delta if we propose a 12% guaranteed buffer + 15% burst pool (best-effort, pre-emptible) instead of a 25% hard reserve?

pete: financially that buys us more flexibility and keeps discounted committed rate intact. We should also model seasonal spikes (Oct–Dec) — they mentioned holiday promotions.

mike: propose a 3-tier: base commit 45k, guaranteed buffer 10–12% for latency-sensitive bursts, and a 20% burst bucket billed at a higher rate when used. Include auto-fallback to hosted multiregion if eu-west saturates.

tom-stormwave: Can you quantify cost delta? They don't want surprise egress or huge overage bills.

pete: rough math: committed 45k GPU hours @ committed rate. A guaranteed 12% buffer effectively reserves ~5.4k hours. A 20% burst bucket consumed at on-demand premium adds variable cost. We can cap monthly billable burst consumption or set an alert threshold.

sarah: technical constraints: KV cache warmup + model shard distribution means warm bursts take 5–15s to reach p95 targets depending on model context length. If they want sub-100ms token p95 for short-chat flows, we need pinned instances (higher cost).

lina: let's draft a concrete offer:
```
commit: 45000 gpu_hours/month
guaranteed_buffer: 12% (pinned capacity for latency-critical paths)
burst_pool: 20% (pre-emptible, cold start allowed)
seasonal_topup: allow 15% for Oct–Dec with 48h notice
SLA: p95 generation latency <= target per policy when on guaranteed_buffer or pinned instances
fallback: route to hosted multiregion after 60s backoff
```

mike: looks good. Add a clause: if burst_pool > 70% consumed in any billing week, trigger capacity review and temporary rate uplift or require notice. Keeps us from silent oversubscription.

tom-stormwave: We can agree to 48h notice for seasonal top-ups. The 70% rule is ok if you give us a predictable uplift rate. Also need clarity on network egress within EU — some large downloads will be heavy.

sarah: note: eu-west egress caps are enforced per VPC. For Dedicated we can provision higher egress but need to schedule with networking and it changes cost. I'll ping infra-bot to open a ticket to reserve egress for their VPC.

infra-bot: created ticket TF-1129 to provision 10Gbps egress in eu-west and flagged network engineering. ETA initial review 2 business days.

pete: I'll run an amortized cost table comparing: committed+12% buffer vs committed+25% hard buffer vs committed+12%+burst. Share numbers by EOD.

lina: action items: 1) sarah to confirm if we can carve 12% pinned in eu-west without breaking current SLAs; 2) pete to produce cost comparison; 3) mike to draft term sheet with 70% burst consumption clause and uplift rates; 4) tom to confirm seasonality windows and egress estimates.

tom-stormwave: thanks — will return numbers on seasonality and egress by tomorrow. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll start the term sheet draft and include a simple usage dashboard requirement so StormWave sees burst consumption in near real-time.

sarah: quick tech caveat — if they request quantized model variants to reduce GPU hours, we can recommend q4_4bit or int8 profiles which cut hours but need validation. Noted for the solutions scoping.

lina: perfect. Keep this thread updated. Once pete has the numbers we'll have a clean offer to present.

tom-stormwave: appreciated — ping me in thread or DM if you need sample traffic traces.

mike: thanks all. :sparkles:
